name: GiddyUp Data overlay style
about: The look, type and motion of GiddyUp Data's video overlays, as values a program can read. STYLE.md beside this file explains each one. Seeded by the brand colours (R131); where it lives R134; contrast R140, R179 (every text at least 7:1, measured), R180 (the palette at 7:1); fonts R135, R143. A Remotion project keeps a copy (AIDrivenVideo: npm run sync-tokens).

color.accentFor: the one accent colour (R51): marks, the click ring, map pins, ticks, the chosen option's outline; shapes only, never text (R180)
color.scrimFor: a full-screen card (ChapterCard): the variant's panel colour over the whole frame, opaque (R179: at 0.92 the screen showed through and the PART 2 title measured 4.0:1; FullScreenTitle used 0.8 black)

light.for: a dark screen (a dark dialog, a dark page)
light.heading: #7b4622

color.waterFor: what flows (SourceFlow's pipe): a light teal from the brand teal on the dark panel, the teal itself on the light one
color.brandFor: the brand's own values (R131); text uses the variant shades below, which are the nearest to these that pass 7:1 (R180)

contrast.for: R179: every text against what is right behind it, measured on the rendered frame (WCAG's enhanced level)
contrast.panelsOpaque: R179 (2026-10-15): no see-through behind any panel; at 96% the dark variant's muted gold over a white screen measured 6.24:1
contrast.wells: a well is the box behind an option or a card's text; it is a near-panel shade so the variant's heading and body keep 7:1 on it, and its rule outline shows its shape

color.mapTint2For: RegionMap's second region tint, also its tag's background under the variant's panel-coloured text (R179: 8.3:1 dark, 7.1:1 light); distinct in hue from mapLit and dot (round 4: mapLines measured 4.85:1 behind a tag)

type.minFor: no text smaller than this at 1080p (R161: a phone held sideways); body and labels at least 56

heading.name: Segoe UI Semibold
heading.for: chapter titles, panel headings, terms, option labels

wordList.name: Segoe Print
wordList.for: a word list or an acronym that builds on the spoken words (R143)

data.name: Courier New
data.for: data: values, formats, field and file names, coordinates (R143)

ofl_standins.note: R148: free OFL fonts, installed on David's PC and bundled with AIDrivenVideo's overlays (remotion/src/overlays/fonts/, licences beside them), so the look holds where the Windows fonts are missing.
ofl_standins.Inter: for Segoe UI and Segoe UI Semibold

type.sizeFor: R161 (2026-10-15): sized for a phone held sideways. Courier New (data) has a small x-height (0.42 em): 52 px of it reads like 44 px of Segoe UI, so data text is never under 52. Captions stay 48 (R126).

layout.safeFor: title-safe at 1080p (R123): what a line refers to sits inside these margins
layout.captionFor: captions (48 px, two lines, R126) sit below this line; an overlay placed by an edge stays above it

graphic.for: R161: a labelled diagram or chart at least this wide (or tall), icons and glyphs at least iconMinPx, strokes at least strokeMinPx, its smallest detail (a bar, a gap) at least detailMinPx

motion.easeFor: a CSS cubic-bezier: a gentle start and a long, soft landing; no overshoot

pop.for: asides only (attention grabbers, R138): David's pop with overshoot
pop.note: the duration is measured from ep03's piggy bank; the peak scale is a starting value, not measured

termChip.what: one line: a term and its meaning, near the thing named

choicePanel.what: two or three options side by side, each on its word; the chosen one outlined orange

wordBuild.what: a list or acronym that builds word by word (Segoe Print), or a data pattern piece by piece (Courier New)

mapPins.what: a USA map: states light, pins with their lat/long, city points with names

highlighter.what: everything but a large region dimmed (R122, R142); its timing lives in the pipeline's settings

miniDiagram.what: boxes and arrows drawn on in order

checklist.what: a stamp and items that tick on their words

aside.what: a drop-in still or clip on its noun, with the pop

flipCard.what: cards that scale up or flip, one after another

calendarFlip.what: a calendar whose months flip: time passing

sourceFlow.what: a data source as a pipe from where the data lives, filling dataset cards; a branch, an upload with no pipe
